adr_corpus: Start a decisions/ folder and record each design decision as a short ADR: what was decided, why, and what it replaced.
design_md_sections: Write a design/DESIGN.md with sections for principles, colour, type, spacing and components, so an agent can read the intent before it writes UI.
token_record_coverage: Document your most-used tokens (what each is for, where it must not be used), starting with colour and type.
adr_recency: Record recent design decisions: the newest decision record is old, so the latest changes have no written reason.
token_record_currency: Update the token records whose documented value no longer matches the token file, or delete the records you no longer maintain.
design_md_currency: Bring the colours listed in DESIGN.md back in line with the token file, so the docs and the code agree.
no_contradictions: Fix the places where the docs describe something the code does not do (a colour format claimed but not used, a generated file that does not exist).
guardrails_file: Write a design/guardrails.mdx: the rules an agent must follow when it writes UI, in plain sentences.
rule_count: Add concrete rules to the guardrails (one rule per bullet): which tokens to use, which components to reuse, what never to hard-code.
starred_rules: Mark the rules you actually enforce, and back each one with a check that runs in CI.
type_size_rule: Add a rule for type sizes: use the type scale, never an arbitrary pixel size.
spacing_scale_rule: Add a rule for spacing: use the spacing scale, never a raw pixel or rem value.
sections: Group the guardrails under headings (colour, type, spacing, components, accessibility) so they are easy to find and extend.
contrast_checked: Fix the colour pairs named in the guardrails that fail WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 for body text).
tokens_css: Keep the design tokens in one canonical file (design/tokens.css, or point systemix.config.yaml at the file you use).
token_source: Create a single token file that declares your colours, type sizes, spacing and radii as CSS custom properties.
palette_classes: Replace the default Tailwind palette classes (bg-blue-500 and friends) with your own semantic colour classes.
font_size_off_token: Replace arbitrary font sizes (text-[13px]) with the type scale, and map that scale into your Tailwind theme.
type_scale_wired: Wire the type tokens you declared into the theme (or use them via var()), or delete the ones nobody uses.
spacing_literals: Replace raw spacing values (px, rem) in components with spacing tokens or the Tailwind spacing scale.
spacing_scale_wired: Wire the spacing tokens you declared into the theme (or use them via var()), or delete the ones nobody uses.
radius_share: Replace hard-coded corner radii with the radius tokens.
canonical_reuse: Use the shared Button, Badge, Card and Input components instead of hand-built copies; start with the files that have the most raw elements.
identical_definitions: Merge the copy-pasted component definitions into one shared component.
single_definitions: Keep one definition of each primitive (Button, Badge, Card, Input) and delete or wrap the local re-implementations.
dead_components: Delete the components nothing imports, or wire them in: dead copies mislead agents into reusing the wrong one.
drift_control_score: Move the raw colour values in components into the token file and reference them from there.
script_exists: Add a drift check script (or the systemix drift scan) to package.json so anyone can run it.
history_recurring: Run the drift check regularly (not once) so you can see whether drift grows or shrinks.
ci_wired: Run the drift check in CI on every pull request.
recent_snapshot: Run the drift check again: the newest snapshot is old.
can_fail_build: Let the drift check fail the build when new raw values appear, so drift is caught before review.
instruction_file: Add an agent instruction file (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md) at the root with how this codebase builds UI.
substance: Expand the agent instruction file: where the tokens and components live, which rules apply, and how to check work.
guardrails_pointer: Tell agents, in the instruction file, to read the guardrails before any UI change.
pointers_resolve: Fix the paths in the instruction files that point to files or folders that do not exist.
no_machine_paths: Remove paths that only exist on one person's machine (~/..., /Users/...) from the instruction files.
fresh_status: Update the status section of the instruction file; it is out of date.
skills_installed: Install the skills your instruction file tells agents to use, or stop naming the ones you do not ship.
